sections.title: The Dimensional Paradox (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: A 1D line has length, but no area.
A 2D square covers a distinct area.
Can a continuous path visit every 2D point?
animations: Fade in 2D square. Color: #FF5733 (Orange-Red). Label: '2D Plane'.
Show a 1D line filling the 2D square. Color: #33FF57 (Light Green). Label: '1D Line'.
Morph line into a space-filling curve. Color: #3357FF (Sky Blue).

sections.title: The Peano Curve Construction (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Start with a single simple line segment.
Split it into smaller sub-segments recursively.
Folding eventually fills the entire 2D area.
animations: Subdivide into nine smaller squares. Color: #CCCCCC (Light Gray).
Connect centers of squares with line segments. Color: #FF00FF (Magenta).

sections.title: The Hilbert Curve & Locality (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: Hilbert curves maintain local spatial relationships.
Points near on curve remain near in 2D.
This locality property optimizes data storage mapping.
A robot gardener minimizes travel with this path.
Complexity emerges from simple recursive rules.

sections.title: Real-World Applications (3:30-4:30)
lecture_lines: Useful for image processing and database indexing.
Optimizes storage for high-speed retrieval tasks.
animations: Visualize image pixel ordering. Color: #FF0000 (Red). Label: 'Pixel Map'.
Show cache-friendly data access. Color: #00FF00 (Green). Label: 'Cache Line'.
Highlight spatial query optimization. Color: #0000FF (Blue). Label: 'Spatial Query'.

sections.title: Summary & Reflection (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Space-filling curves bridge different dimensional worlds.
They transform multi-dimensional data into linear sequences.
Recursion builds beauty from simple iterative loops.
animations: List core concepts (Dimension, Recursion, Locality). Color: #FFFFFF (White).
Highlight the connection between dimensions. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
Show final infinite curve. Color: #00FFFF (Cyan). Label: 'Space-filling'.
